title: A knock on the head — watch them for hours, not minutes
applies_to: Anyone who has hit their head in a fall, a crash, a fight, or a game.

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: First Aid
citations.section: Head injury, cervical spine motion restriction

steps.text: Ask them their name, where they are, and what happened. Muddled answers matter far more than the size of the lump.
Call for an ambulance if they blacked out. Call if they cannot remember the knock, are being sick again and again, or are getting harder to wake.
Keep them sitting or lying still and quiet, with the head and shoulders raised a little.
If the scalp is bleeding, press a clean cloth firmly on it. Scalp wounds bleed a lot and still press to a stop.
Put something cold, wrapped in cloth, on a lump for up to 20 minutes.
Watch them closely for the next 24 hours. Someone should stay with them. That person must be able to wake them easily.
Watch for these signs. A headache that keeps growing. Being sick. Blurred sight. Slurred speech. Weakness down one side.
Go to a hospital at once if any of those signs show up. Go even if it is a day or two later.
Get them seen today anyway if they are very young or very old. Go too if they had been drinking, or take something that thins the blood.

do_not: Do not let them go back to a game, to work at height, or behind the wheel.
Do not leave them on their own for the first 24 hours.
Do not press hard on a soft or dented part of the skull.
Do not move them if the neck may be hurt, unless they are choking or being sick.
Do not let them drink alcohol while you are watching them.
escalate_if: Clear fluid or blood runs from the nose or from an ear — call an ambulance now.
One pupil looks bigger than the other, or they cannot stay awake — call now.
They start shaking or jerking — protect the head and let it run its course.
They stop answering you but are breathing normally — roll them onto their side.
They become angry, restless, or make no sense — that is a warning sign, not bad behaviour.
